blocks.content: The consultation with the Chief Justice of India in the appointment of judges means concurrence, establishing the primacy of the judiciary.

rows: Consultation does not mean concurrence; Executive retains final primacy.
Consultation means concurrence; CJI + 2 senior judges form Collegium.
Expanded Collegium to CJI + 4 senior-most judges for Supreme Court appointments.
Struck down 99th Amendment & NJAC to restore the Collegium system.

items: The term 'Consultation' was officially interpreted as 'Concurrence' in the Second Judges Case (1993).
The qualification category of 'Distinguished Jurist' exists only for Supreme Court judge appointments, not for High Courts.
The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act and NJAC Act were declared unconstitutional for violating the basic structure (judicial independence).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed by the President of India.
The Collegium System evolved through three major judicial precedents: First (1981), Second (1993), and Third (1998) Judges Cases.
For Supreme Court appointments, the Collegium comprises the Chief Justice of India and four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court.
The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act establishing the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) was struck down in the Fourth Judges Case (2015).
Qualifications for SC judges require Indian citizenship and 5 years as an HC judge, 10 years as an HC advocate, or being a distinguished jurist.
